title: Volume 1 Chapter 2: Nail Machine 1
content: So, here I am, Hajime Azuma, having received a request from my classmate, the dragon girl Sayori Goto, to be her personal nail artist. I had only made nail chips for her once. My knowledge of nails is still lacking, and I haven't even solved the issue of Sayori's sturdy dragon claws. In a situation where I can't even apply polish, there's no way I can call myself a nail artist.
But still. I want to do what I can for Sayori. I've decided never to say it's impossible or that I can't do it. From now on, I’ll consult with Sayori in earnest and try various things for her nails.

Now, with that in mind, there’s only one thing to do. My home is about a twenty-minute bike ride from the garage. Usually, after school, I stop by the garage before heading home. My mother often tells me to come home earlier. The reason is simple. According to her, dinner is something the whole family should eat together. Although we don't have much conversation as a family, we often gather for dinner.
“Dad.”
After dinner, I called out to my father, who was tilting his glass of whiskey, his favorite drink.
“What is it, Hajime?”
He replied in a low voice. I don’t dislike my father. I’m grateful that he lets me use the garage, and I respect his skills as a craftsman, able to finish everything from pain cars to niche vehicles.

However, that doesn’t mean our conversations flow easily. My father is, after all, just like me—an introvert, quiet and not very good at talking. I know from experience that when two quiet people try to converse, misunderstandings and miscommunications are bound to happen. So, I always feel tense when talking to him.
“It’s about the garage.”
“Oh, did something happen?”
“Um... I’m going to have friends over frequently from now on.”
After hesitating over how much to explain about Sayori, I ended up saying it that way.
“I’d like to leave some tools related to that.”
“Tools? I assume they’re for plastic models. You can use whatever I’ve lent you freely. Just make sure to tell your friends not to touch the tools and paints for cars.”
My father dislikes having his work tools touched. While there are dangers like poisoning from the paints, the bigger reason is that he’s a craftsman with strong preferences.
“Ah, that’s not it... I want to leave some tools that I won’t use for plastic models.”
“? I don’t understand. Speak clearly.”
When my father said that directly, I felt like my head was spinning. I wanted to get permission without mentioning nails, but that seemed difficult.
“Well, actually, I’ve been asked by a female friend to do her nails.”
I decided to give in and convey it without trying to hide it.
“Nails... you mean the stuff you put on your fingers?”
“Exactly. So, I want to use the garage as my workspace... and I’ll probably have my female friend over often, so I want to leave various tools for that...”
“Why me?”
“I’m not sure myself, but it seems nails and plastic models have a lot in common...”
“Dad, is that okay?”
The reason I can use the garage is that my father allows it, and I keep my promise not to touch his work tools. Since the purpose of the garage is going to change, I need to inform him.
If I stay silent and he finds out later, I might end up losing the garage altogether.
“...Nails, huh. I don’t understand it at all, but...”
Taking a sip of whiskey, my father pondered. “As long as it’s within the range I’ve lent you, feel free to use it. But I’ll say it again, make sure your friends don’t touch the tools for cars.”
“Ah, thanks, Dad.”
“And if a girl is coming over, don’t stay out too late.”
I nodded. I wondered if Sayori had a curfew; she certainly didn’t look like someone who would be out late at night.
Anyway, I had received permission to use the garage. I would be consulting with Sayori about nails in earnest from now on. I also needed to gather nail tools and paints.
Fortunately, from what I saw while shopping the other day, nail supplies don’t seem to be that expensive. If I go regularly, I should be able to gather everything without much trouble.
“What girl? Who!? A classmate!?”

The problem was that my mother, who was washing dishes, latched onto this topic and began asking a lot of questions. Unlike my father and me, she’s quite the chatterbox and seems to thrive on conversation.
While I countered her inquiries with silence, I was thinking about the tools I needed to gather for nails.

It was a relief to be able to invite Sayori to the garage without hesitation. Still, I had many concerns regarding her nails. While I had found a solution in nail chips, Sayori herself was particular about nail polish.
“Excuse me~!”
After school, while I was working in the garage, Sayori arrived a bit late. For the past few days, she had been coming to the garage almost every day. She shared what she had researched about nails.
“Azuma-kun! Today, I pulled out some magazines I had at home!”

Sayori took out a sparkling fashion magazine aimed at girls from her tote bag. Each one was quite thick. Perhaps it was because they were printed in full color. She pulled them out one after another and lined them up on the desk.
“Oh, that must have been heavy.”
“Super heavy! Like, way too much! Have I lost weight!?”
Whether or not she had lost weight was debatable, but there was definitely sweat on Sayori’s forehead.
“So, I marked the pages about nails that caught my eye, so I think we should start from there!”
Indeed, there were several sticky notes attached to the heavier magazines.
In a way, I had come to realize that while Sayori seemed to not care about the finer details, she was quite diligent in these matters.
“I hope there are some hints in there.”
“Yeah! Oh, look, look! This one is cute!”
Sayori quickly opened a magazine and showed me a detailed nail design. It featured deep indigo nails with some fish-shaped parts glued on. It seemed to be themed around an aquarium.
—Nails are quite diverse.
“That’s still beyond my skill level.”
“Eh? I totally think you can do it!”
“I can’t even imagine how to make that.”
As I continued to browse through the magazine, I found various types of nails.

There were sparkling nails reminiscent of rhinestones and crystals. There were animal-themed designs like zebra, giraffe, and leopard patterns. Then there were the so-called “oshi nails,” inspired by anime characters. (The desire to express one’s favorites seems to be universal...)

I felt a deep sense of admiration as I looked at the lineup of oshi nails. My father also makes pain cars with anime character stickers in the garage when he gets orders. It’s somewhat amusing to see my quiet father, who knows nothing about anime or games, diligently creating pain cars.
“In any case, there are so many!”
“Right! This is who I am! This is what I like! It’s like a self-expression that gets me hyped!”
“I understand that well.”

The magazine featured various nail examples, much like a catalog of model magazine examples. Addresses of nail salons were noted in the corners, indicating that one could get the same nails done at those salons. (Like, love, and getting hyped... I see.)

All the nails that Sayori seemed to like had sticky notes attached to them. For example, there were comments like “I love this!” “So cute!” “This is seriously amazing!” and “This is seriously seriously amazing!” written on each sticky note.
Well, regardless of her vocabulary, by looking at this, I could understand Sayori’s favorite nails—and ultimately, what kind of person she is.
Self-expression, indeed.
(That said, there’s still the issue of design—)
While I had a good grasp of Sayori’s preferences, that was that. As I flipped through the pages, the nail examples ended, and nail supplies were introduced.
The first thing that caught my eye was...
“Oh, that’s a nail dryer!”
Sayori exclaimed excitedly.
“A nail dryer?”
It was a somewhat sci-fi-looking device. A white dome-shaped machine with a hole in the center. Purple light was glowing from the top part of the dome.
“If you put your hand in here, it dries faster than air drying! And it can also emit light to cure gel nails...”
I had seen the term gel nails occasionally while researching nails, but I didn’t quite understand what it was.
“Oh, well! Nails can be broadly divided into polish and gel! With gel, you can freely design until you cure it with UV light! Most of what’s in this catalog is gel nails!”
“Ah, so it’s UV-curable resin.”
Sayori tilted her head.
“We use it in plastic models to make clear parts. It’s a bit of a hassle, so I don’t use it much—”
“Really!?”
“By the way, there’s also a UV light curing machine in the back.”
“Wow... So, are modelers also nail artists?”
“No.”
Well, if you’re using UV-curable resin, it makes sense to use a UV light. It was probably just a coincidence.
I was becoming interested in gel nails, but I felt that it was still a high hurdle for me. I’m not very good at working with resin in plastic models either.
However, as I turned to the next page of the magazine—there was something familiar again.
“Nail machine!”
Sayori eagerly explained everything. While I appreciated it, our faces were close since we were looking at the same magazine.
“This is the thing that peels off cured gel! Once it hardens, it doesn’t come off easily!”
“Oh, I see, if it’s cured resin, that makes sense—”
The nail machine, it seems, is a pen-shaped device with a stick-shaped file attached to the tip, which rotates to remove gel nails. The main body appears to be a motor.
The mechanism itself is quite simple, but—
“It’s so nice! The nail machine looks cute... It feels like a tool specialized for nails! It’s professional, like someone designed it just for gel nails... Isn’t it emotional!?”
Sayori was lost in thought about the creator of the nail machine.
I think her unique sensitivity is wonderful. I do, but to me, this nail machine looks like—
“No, it’s a hand grinder.”
“Huh... grind...?”
“Grinder. It’s a tool for drilling holes and sanding in plastic models.”
I took out my hand grinder, which I always use, from the desk drawer.

It was likely a bit larger than the nail machine featured in the magazine, but the basic structure was the same. By changing the tip—the attachment part according to the purpose, various processes can be easily achieved.
“Is this a nail machine!? Oh, it’s a bit bulky, though.”
“Well, it’s for plastic models, after all...”
The nail machine in the magazine also clearly had the same mechanism as a grinder.
If you’re removing UV-curable resin, you could consider the nail machine as being for plastic as well.
It seems the machine in the magazine can also adjust the rotation speed, but my grinder can do that too.
“Isn’t the garage basically a nail salon!?”
“No, it’s not.”
That said, with UV-curable resin and grinders, the more I researched, the more I realized that common techniques are used in both nails and plastic models.
“Hmmm...”
It’s true that removing resin from nails would be impossible with a regular nail file. A specialized machine is necessary.
Conversely, one could think that sturdy nails could be ground down with a hand grinder—right?
“Hey, Sayori... should we try using this to grind your nails?”
I asked cautiously.
“Eh? Is that okay? Do you think it’ll work?”
“We won’t know until we try—”
After all, it’s not a machine meant for nails.
“You can also wrap diamond file paper around the tip and use it, so theoretically, it should grind properly. What usually takes an hour to polish could be done much faster with a grinder.”
Originally, I thought it wouldn’t be appropriate to use a machine on nails, even if she is a dragon girl—but...
If we have a nail machine, this grinder should work too.
“Hmmm, well, they say you won’t know until you try? Should we just go for it?”
“Is that okay? Aren’t you scared?”
I made sure to confirm.
It wouldn’t be surprising to be apprehensive about using a machine to grind nails. Especially since I’m not a professional nail artist.
“Well, if it’s you, Azuma-kun, who’s skilled enough to make nail chips, you’ll be totally fine! Let’s do it!”
With a carefree declaration, Sayori began clearing away the magazines lined up on the desk.
(...Does this mean she trusts me?)
It seems she has faith in my skills.
That’s troubling. With her saying this much, I absolutely cannot fail.
As a modeler, I must ensure success.
I faced Sayori across the desk once more.
I reached out to touch her middle finger, which I had polished before. Her nail had a rough texture.

(Already the rough texture has returned...) It's only been about ten days since then. If I’m going to keep doing nails regularly, Sayori's dragon claws will need to be polished periodically. (Well, I hope the grinder can solve that.) I sincerely wished my trusty hand grinder would show its true power.
[img]https://i.imgur.com/CpJV6PV.jpeg
“So, what do we do first?”
“Ah, first... I’ll wrap sandpaper around the bit.”
I took out the diamond sandpaper and cut it to fit the size of the replacement attachment—the bit.
“Huh? Wrap sandpaper... why?”
“There are sanding bits for grinders, but... I don’t think they’ll work on Sayori’s nails. I want to use diamond-coated sandpaper, so I’ll do it this way.”
I attached double-sided tape to an unused bit and began wrapping the sandpaper around it. With this method, even if the sandpaper loses its abrasive power, I can easily swap it out for a new one.
“I think they sell diamond bits for glass processing too, but... I don’t have any on hand, so I’ll stick with this method for now.”
“Okay, I’ll leave it to you♪”
Her straightforwardness was a relief. It was likely her trust in me that made her so open—there was no way I could let her get hurt.
I set the grinder’s rotation speed and turned it on. The bit began to spin with a sound.
Now, let’s see if it can actually grind...
“I’ll go slowly, but if it hurts, tell me right away.”
I didn’t think it would come to that, but if I accidentally ground down her flesh along with her nails, it would be a disaster.
“Y-yeah.”
Maybe my seriousness got through to her, as Sayori held her breath.
I carefully pressed the spinning grinder’s tip against her nail, hovering just above it.
“Hmm.”
Sayori let out a small sound.
“Did it hurt?”
“No, it’s fine. It just tickled a bit.”
“Oh, I see—”
Doesn’t this conversation sound a bit suggestive? I quickly shook off the noise in my head. I’m doing this for her nails, focus, Azuma!
Taking a deep breath, I pressed the grinder’s tip against her nail again. The friction between the nail and the sandpaper made a sound.
(...It’s working!)
Golden shavings floated up as fine dust.
“Hey, how’s it feeling?”
Sayori seemed to catch on, smiling at me.
“Yeah, using the machine makes a huge difference.”
“Yay♪ Is it really this good from the start? I should’ve used it earlier!”
“No, I never thought to use it on nails...”
It was only after learning about the existence of nail machines that I realized my hand grinder could be useful.
I still had a lot to learn about nails, but it seemed that the knowledge I had from model making could be applied to a fair extent.
That said, the amount of shavings produced was still minimal, and it was clear that Sayori’s nails were tough.
“I’ll be careful, so don’t move.”
“Okay♪”
After that—
I gently brushed the grinder against Sayori’s nails, checking to see if I was grinding properly—repeating this process for all her fingers.
With the grinder making it easier to grind, the sandpaper wore out quickly. After just ten minutes of work, the surface of the diamond file was already worn down.
While swapping out the sandpaper I had wrapped around the tip as needed, I fought with it for about an hour—
“...Did I finish?”
Finally, I had ground down all her nails.
“Wow... they feel a bit smoother, I think!”
Sayori touched her nails and expressed her fluffy impression.
Still, if the texture had changed that much, I could consider it a success for now. The power of the machine was indeed great.
“Can we put polish on now!?”
“Probably... should we give it a try?”
I picked up a small bottle of nail polish I had bought for testing.
Since it was just a trial, I applied a little to the tip—just as I expected, the paint didn’t crack like before and vividly colored Sayori’s nails.
“Is this... a success!? It’s a success, right!?”
“Yeah, it’s forming a nice coating...”
“Yay~! I can finally do my nails! I can finally have nails~!”
“Hey, don’t move yet.”
Sayori was trembling with excitement, her hands still posed in front of her.
If left unchecked, she would probably jump around in joy again, so I had to rein her in.
“No way, this is impossible! Until now, I’ve just been admiring cute polish! From now on, I can paint as much as I want! This is the best!”
“—I’m glad for you.”
For a human, it’s just a matter of buying a bottle of nail polish and applying it.
It’s simple, and the price isn’t particularly high. That’s why even students can easily give it a try. It might even be less of a hurdle than makeup.
That’s why Sayori’s struggle to not be able to do her nails must have been quite significant.
“Well, you can paint them yourself now. Choose your favorite color.”
“I don’t want to! I want you to do it, Azuma-kun!”
“Why not...?”
It was just a matter of applying the paint, so she should be able to do it by herself.
But Sayori flashed a grin.
“I’m not good at it!”
“Don’t say that with such confidence.”
“You’ll definitely paint it much prettier than I could! You’re my personal nail artist, so please do it!”
“Alright, alright...”
For some reason, I was weak against the word “personal.”
Maybe it made me feel like my dexterity and modeler skills were being praised. No, I was doing nails, but still.
“Okay, think about what color you want. We don’t have time to paint today, so we’ll do it tomorrow.”
It was already close to six o’clock. My father had warned me, so staying late wasn’t a good idea.
“Okay! I have lots of polish at home, so I’ll bring some tomorrow!”
“...Did you buy them even though you couldn’t paint?”
“Because! They’re all so cute and colorful!”
Sayori asserted strongly.
She had gathered many bottles of polish that she couldn’t use. What kind of feelings did she have while looking at those colorful bottles?
“Well, from now on, I’ll paint whatever you want. Bring your favorite colors.”
“Yeah! I’ll leave it to you! Azuma-kun, see you tomorrow!”
With that, Sayori cheerfully left the garage.
The sound of her footsteps echoed in the garage. Was she planning to run back to the station?
(...Tomorrow again, huh?)
I had always been alone in this garage.
It was naturally my workspace, but I never imagined I would have someone to promise to meet again.
(I guess I’ll do my best again tomorrow.)
I began to clean up. Gathering the shavings and putting the tools back in their original places. It was something I always did, but this time I did it more carefully.
I might have to grind Sayori’s nails again. I decided to prepare several bits wrapped with sandpaper in advance. If I wrapped them one by one in front of Sayori, it would take too long.
(I need to replenish my supplies.)
Considering the strength of Sayori’s nails, having a stock would be better.
As I cleaned and prepared for the next day, I truly felt that this place had become a space to welcome clients.
Preparing before working on models is important. I figured nails would be the same.
Everything was for the sake of warmly welcoming Sayori again in this garage tomorrow.
After returning home, I found myself troubled.
(I bought it...)
My room was simple, with a study desk, a few model examples, a bed, a game console, and a TV.
Most of my hobby items were in the garage, so it was quite minimal.
On top of the study desk, something that didn’t quite fit in this simple room was sitting there.
It was a fashion magazine aimed at women.
(...I wonder what the convenience store clerk thought.)
I regretted it, worrying that it might seem strange, as I was quite the introvert.
This fashion magazine likely contained photos of Sayori Goto as a model. I had bought it without thinking deeply, hoping to use it as a reference for nails.
—Reading this in my room, doesn’t it seem creepy?
(Didn’t it look like I bought the magazine just to see Sayori...?)
I quickly shook off the thoughts that popped into my head. This was purely for reference for Sayori’s nails.
Feeling a bit embarrassed, I began flipping through the pages.
I quickly found the page featuring Sayori. There was a fashion corner for dragons and other demi-human women.
(...There are so many demi-humans.)
Dragon demi-humans. Cat demi-humans. Wolf demi-humans. Cow demi-humans. Oni.
There were that many demi-humans on just one page.
Each had a model, and each had fashion photos that suited them.
It seems that having horns, beast ears, or tails changes the fashion that suits them.
(What kind of demi-human is this?)
On another page, there was even a photo of a woman with blue skin and four arms.
She looked like a god or a demon from a game.
I had heard that there were over a hundred types of demi-humans—but seeing them like this, I realized there were many I didn’t know.
(As for Sayori...)
Sayori Goto was dressed in a refreshing gal outfit suitable for dragons for the upcoming season.
As always, she wore clothes that exposed her belly. I guess she likes that.
As for nails—she wasn’t wearing any. Naturally.
If Sayori had been able to do her nails freely, would she have matched them to this outfit? She probably never imagined she would be doing nails with me during the shoot.
(Hmm?)
I suddenly noticed.

Upon closer inspection, it seemed that other demi-humans weren’t wearing nails either. Well, the cat demi-human’s claws looked completely different from human ones. Sharp claws extended from their furry hands. I wondered if they could even be painted.
There might be many demi-human girls like Sayori who struggled with their nails.
(It must have been tough not being able to do nails...)
I couldn’t understand it at all—but for Sayori, nails seemed to be an essential part of her.
If I were banned from painting models, I might make a face like that too.
I looked again at Sayori’s photo.
In the picture, Sayori had a more serious and cool expression than when we talked in the garage. The model introduction described her as a charismatic dragon girl.
Charismatic—does she really have that?
(She can make that kind of expression too...)
She looked like she wasn’t thinking about anything in the garage.
I had heard she was a reader model, but I was impressed that she could make such a professional expression. It made me feel like she was from a different world than mine.
So, it felt strange that I would meet this model in the garage tomorrow.
The Sayori in the photo was both like Sayori and not like her. I felt that the model Sayori was just one aspect of her, which changed as she expressed herself.
I flipped through the magazine casually.
demi-human models were just a part of it; the majority were ordinary human fashion models. I didn’t know much about clothes, so I skimmed through.
I did check the nails of other models carefully, but—
Since the photos were primarily focused on the clothes, there were few where the nails were clearly visible. Many of the models’ nails were simple.
Even if there were intricate designs, the angles were often pulled back, making it difficult to capture the nails clearly.
(This is definitely different from the nail catalog I saw today.)
It must be a difference between whether the clothes or the nails are the main focus.
Which means—
It seems that depending on Sayori’s mood or the occasion, such simple nails would also become necessary.
After that, I continued to glance at the fashion magazine, checking the models’ nails. I was thinking about how to apply this to Sayori’s nails, considering various ideas.
(I wonder what she’s thinking about what to paint right now.)
I suddenly thought of Sayori.
She must have a mountain of polishes she wants to use. Whether they’re simple ones for such shoots or something unique.
Well, I’ll just do my best to meet her expectations.
Before I knew it, I realized I was looking forward to what kind of nails she would suggest next.
And then—
